do_not_assume: A staff-session route is suitable for public use.
Settings observed in another installation exist here.
goal: A bounded map of the current application flow and its security-sensitive surfaces.
steps: Record the installed Rock version and whether Helix is core- or plugin-provided.
Inspect the Lava Application’s name, description, slug, configuration rigging, activity state, and security.
Identify every linked Lava Application Content block.
Inventory the application’s endpoints by name, slug, method, and activity state.
For each endpoint, record security mode, enabled commands, caching, code-template purpose, and any exposed rate-limit or CSRF setting.
Trace each page action to its endpoint and target element.
Identify which endpoints read, mutate, delete, or launch other work.
Review representative observability activities before altering behavior.
title: Recipe: Inspect an existing Helix application before changing it

do_not_assume: Read-only behavior makes private fields safe to expose.
A default cache policy is appropriate for person-specific output.
goal: A page-hosted query interaction that returns only authorized display content.
steps: Create or select a Lava Application with a documented name, description, and slug.
Add a GET endpoint for the result fragment.
Configure its security mode for the intended audience.
Enable only the Lava commands required to read and render the result.
Validate and allowlist all query values.
Check the caller’s right to view each protected entity.
Add a Lava Application Content block and link it to the application.
Render useful initial content.
Add the HTMX request using a caret route and an explicit target.
Test empty, invalid, unauthorized, and representative result states.
Inspect endpoint traces and database calls.
title: Recipe: Build a read-only HTMX result fragment

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: A non-GET endpoint that rejects unauthorized or invalid direct calls as well as invalid browser submissions.
steps: Place the controls inside `<lava-form>`.
Prefer supplied Helix control shortcodes where they meet the requirement.
Add native validation rules and clear validation messages.
Use POST, PUT, or DELETE according to the operation.
Configure endpoint or application execution security.
Enable only the commands needed for the mutation.
Repeat every validation rule in the endpoint.
Resolve the target entity from validated input.
Verify the caller’s edit rights to that entity.
Parameterize or sanitize any SQL inputs.
If multiple writes must succeed together, assess the DB Transaction command.
Return an appropriate status or HTMX response instruction.
Test the endpoint directly with missing, malformed, unauthorized, and tampered input.
title: Recipe: Build a validated mutation form

do_not_assume: Do not rely on the default GET method for any mutation.
goal: Endpoint-generated content appears during the initial page render without a second request or avoidable layout shift.
steps: Confirm the installed version supports `renderlavaendpoint`.
Select a read-safe endpoint for the initial render.
Invoke it with the caret route.
Specify the method when it is not GET.
Do not rely on the default GET method for any mutation.
Compare the initial output with the later HTMX-rendered fragment.
Confirm authorization behaves consistently in both contexts.
Measure whether the extra-request and layout-shift problem is resolved.
title: Recipe: Render endpoint content on first paint

do_not_assume: A successful HTTP response proves correct data semantics.
goal: Evidence that source targeting, authorization, data semantics, interaction behavior, and responsive layout all work in the actual page context.
steps: Confirm the saved application, endpoint, and Content block source matches the intended source.
Open the rendered page as an unauthorized visitor.
Test as the intended role.
Test as an administrator, but record that result separately.
Assert known totals or invariants and representative rows.
Exercise each filter, sort, refresh, and empty state.
Inspect visible errors, hidden Lava error surfaces, network failures, and console errors.
Test narrow and wide layouts for clipped labels, unintended internal scrolling, and unbounded horizontal overflow.
Inspect endpoint traces for representative requests.
title: Recipe: Validate a rendered Helix dashboard

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: A documented decision to retain Helix or move to a purpose-built solution.
steps: Count the application’s endpoints.
Identify whether the requested design requires custom models.
Assess whether ordinary changes are becoming complex or fragile.
Review security, deployment, testing, and maintenance costs.
If custom models, approximately 50 or more endpoints, or persistent fragility are present, compare a purpose-built implementation.
Keep the application in Helix only when its operational boundaries remain understandable and supportable.
title: Recipe: Decide whether to replace a Lava Application
